note: Confirmed only by a 2023 news report; no official cemetery page was found. Tour dates vary.
hours: Open grounds; twilight history tours some seasons.

name: Studebaker-Bendix Heritage Trail
what: A self-guided driving tour of 13 sites tied to the Studebaker and Bendix companies, from the carriage-factory site downtown to Bendix Woods. It takes about 90 minutes.
research: Developed by Visit South Bend Mishawaka with the Historic Preservation Commission, Indiana Landmarks, the county parks and the two museums.
address: Starts at S. Michigan St. & E. Jefferson Blvd., South Bend
note: The link is the visitors' bureau page that produced the trail.

name: Bendix Woods County Park
what: A county park on the former Studebaker proving-ground land. The original Studebaker clubhouse, now a nature centre, and a 1930s pine-tree planting that spells STUDEBAKER are both listed on the National Register.
note: sjcparks.org refused the fetch (robots). The visitors' bureau page confirms the park and its features.

name: University of Notre Dame historic campus (Eck Visitors Center)
what: Free public walking tours of the historic campus start at the Eck Visitors Center. Stops include the Main Building (Golden Dome), the Basilica of the Sacred Heart, the Grotto, the Log Chapel and Cedar Grove Cemetery.
address: Eck Visitors Center, next to the Hammes Bookstore, Notre Dame Ave. entrance, Notre Dame, IN 46556
note: Register in person within 30 minutes of a tour; first 25 people only. Hours not posted.
hours: Free walking tours from the visitors center; sign up in person.

name: Heritage and Research Center (HARC), Saint Mary's College
what: A new shared archive for the Sisters of the Holy Cross and nine other women's religious congregations, with a permanent exhibit space and a rotating one.
research: Finding aids are online at harc.libraryhost.com.
address: Saint Mary's College, Notre Dame, IN 46556
note: Grand opening was 26 May 2026; full public opening is in 2027. Until then visits are by appointment.
hours: By appointment until it opens fully in 2027.

name: Morris Performing Arts Center
what: A restored 1922 vaudeville and movie palace, built as the Palace Theatre, now the city's main performing-arts venue.
address: 211 N. Michigan St., South Bend, IN 46601
note: The site has a 'Tours' link, but no tour schedule was found.
hours: Open for performances; ask about tours.

name: Lerner Theatre
what: A 1924 downtown theatre with its original Kimball organ, listed on the National Register in 1980 and still used for performances.
note: Guided 'Behind the Curtain' tours are offered occasionally ($10). There are free lunchtime organ concerts.
hours: Open for performances; occasional behind-the-scenes tours.

name: Coppes Commons and Coppes History Museum
what: The 1876 Coppes Napanee factory, once a maker of Hoosier kitchen cabinets, now a marketplace and working cabinet shop with a history museum. In 2026 a 30-foot Hoosier-cabinet replica was added to mark the company's 150th year.
research: The museum holds archives and catalogs on Hoosier cabinet makers.
note: Generally 10–5 Eastern. The full weekly schedule is on the site.

name: Krider "World's Fair" Garden Park
what: A town park preserving the Krider Nurseries garden exhibit from the 1933–34 Chicago World's Fair, with its original garden features.
note: Public park, open seasonally. The town page confirms only the 1934 fair.

name: Historic Goshen Walking Tour
what: A self-guided walk of about one mile (60–90 minutes) through downtown Goshen and the Elkhart County Courthouse square, prepared by the Goshen Historical Society.
address: Centred on Main St.; the museum at 124 S. Main St., Goshen, IN is a natural start
note: Year-round. The museum itself is already in your directory; this is the separate trail.

name: Bristol Opera House
what: A historic small-town opera house, restored by and home to the Elkhart Civic Theatre.
note: Open for performances. The construction year (believed to be the 1890s) was not confirmed on the page.

name: Cass District Library – Main Branch
what: The main library of the system that serves most of Cass County’s townships, with Ancestry Library Edition for family history.
research: Local history is kept at the Local History Branch on Broadway.
hours: See the library’s website for hours.

name: Cass District Library – Edwardsburg Branch
what: A branch of the Cass District Library.
hours: See the library’s website for hours.

name: Cass District Library – Mason/Union Branch
what: A branch of the Cass District Library.
hours: See the library’s website for hours.

name: Cass District Library – Howard Branch
what: A branch of the Cass District Library.
hours: See the library’s website for hours.

name: Marcellus Township Wood Memorial Library
what: The township library for the Village of Marcellus and Marcellus Township.
research: Bound copies of the Marcellus News, 1995–2024, which staff will scan for you.
